answer_text:
Let

\[
pqrs+1=4^{p+q}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad pqrs=4^{p+q}-1.
\]

First note that none of \(p,q,r,s\) can be \(2\). If one of them were \(2\), then \(pqrs\) would be even, so \(pqrs+1\) would be odd, while \(4^{p+q}\) is even. Contradiction. Thus all four primes are odd.

Now reduce modulo \(3\). Since \(4\equiv 1\pmod 3\),

\[
4^{p+q}-1\equiv 1^{p+q}-1\equiv 0\pmod 3.
\]

So \(3\mid pqrs\). Hence one of the primes is \(3\). Since \(p\) is the smallest, we must have

\[
p=3.
\]

Now \(q\) is an odd prime greater than \(3\), so \(p+q=3+q\) is even. Reduce modulo \(5\). Since \(4\equiv -1\pmod 5\),

\[
4^{p+q}-1\equiv (-1)^{\text{even}}-1\equiv 1-1\equiv 0\pmod 5.
\]

Thus \(5\mid pqrs\). Since the primes are ordered \(p<q<r<s\) and \(p=3\), the next prime factor must be

\[
q=5.
\]

Substitute \(p=3\), \(q=5\):

\[
3\cdot 5\cdot r\cdot s+1=4^{3+5}=4^8.
\]

Since \(4^8=65536\),

\[
15rs+1=65536,
\]

so

\[
15rs=65535
\]

and therefore

\[
rs=\frac{65535}{15}=4369.
\]

Factor \(4369\):

\[
4369=17\cdot 257.
\]

Both \(17\) and \(257\) are prime, and \(5<17<257\), so

\[
r=17,\qquad s=257.
\]

Thus

\[
r+s=17+257=274.
\]

\[
\boxed{274}
\]
